subject: Live checkout: streaming metadata dropout causing payment failures - exec escalated
messages:
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@checkoutland.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: support+ops@checkoutland.com
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 08:17:23 -0700
Subject: Live checkout spikes — requests dropping metadata causing payment failures

Hi Rafael,

We're seeing a sharp regression hitting our live checkout beginning around 07:58 PDT. P95 looks OK but p99 latency spikes to 9s and ~2% of checkout POSTs are failing with downstream payment timeouts. Our logs show requests arriving at our gateway missing the "x-rw-meta" streaming frames intermittently — they show up in the client but appear truncated before reaching your backend.

Attached: checkout-p99-trace-20270522.log (excerpted).

This started immediately after we rolled the SDK patch that rolled into our build last night (sdk v1.3.4). Can you confirm whether there's any known issue with streaming metadata frames / client-side dechunking? This is blocking orders. We need an ETA on a mitigation.

Thanks — Alyssa
Alyssa Chen
Head of Payments Engineering, Checkoutland
alyssa@checkoutland.com

Alyssa — thanks for the fast report and the logs. We see the same signature in our ingress traces: intermittent zero-length metadata frames are being stripped by the client-side dechunker before the request envelope is completed, which leaves downstream services without required payment metadata.

Immediate actions:
- I've looped in Marcus (ingest/runtime) and Neha (customer ops) to triage.
- Marcus: can you confirm reproducibility and a short-term patch?
- Neha: please prepare an exec brief — this is high severity for Checkoutland (SLA exposure).

Customer impact: orders can fail payment auth when metadata is missing. We should treat as potential financial impact and escalate to execs if we cannot get a fix or mitigation within 4 hours.

Subject: Re: Live checkout spikes — requests dropping metadata causing payment failures

Quick triage notes (repro steps and short-term mitigation):

What I reproduced:
- With SDK v1.3.4 and a specific batching configuration (batch_size > 8, sequence coalescing enabled), the dechunker can coalesce frames and accidentally drop 0-length metadata frames when a header/trailer boundary aligns with a stream coalescing window. The result: the request body proceeds but the metadata key/value pairs are omitted on the server-side request.

Root cause hypothesis:
- The dechunker state machine incorrectly treats a zero-length metadata frame as a no-op during certain coalescing paths. This is a client-side bug in the buffer flush logic.

Short-term mitigations we can push (order of preference):
1) Ask Checkoutland to pin SDK to v1.3.3 (rollback) — lowest risk and fastest.
2) Server-side fallback: accept requests with missing metadata and try to synthesize from KV-cache when available (best-effort; may increase false negatives).
3) Apply traffic policy: route Checkoutland traffic to a single-connection path (disable coalescing) to avoid the boundary condition.

I have a one-line patch ready for the SDK dechunker: PR #482 (fixes the zero-length metadata handling). If we approve a canary we can cut v1.3.5 in ~90 minutes and provide a customer upgrade note.

I will open an internal postmortem ticket and attach trace examples.

Marcus
Sr. Systems Engineer, Runtime
marcus_lin@redwood.com

Subject: Exec brief: Checkoutland live incident affecting checkout payments (SLA risk)

Team — exec brief for visibility and next-step approvals. Summarized below; please escalate to CRO and CTO immediately if you are the on-call executive.

Summary:
- Impact: Checkoutland (large retail customer) experiencing p99 latency spikes and ~2% payment failures since 07:58 PDT. Root cause traced to client SDK dechunker dropping metadata frames under specific coalescing conditions (sdk v1.3.4).
- Customer risk: Potential lost orders and SLA breach. They run high-volume weekend traffic.
- Likely cause: client-side bug in SDK; Redwood server-side cannot reliably reconstruct missing per-request metadata.

Recommended immediate actions (requires exec sign-off on credits/traffic policy):
1) Approve targeted traffic policy to route Checkoutland to our single-connection path (reduces throughput but prevents coalescing-induced loss). Estimated impact: ~10-20% higher CPU/cost for Checkoutland traffic.
2) Approve issuing a goodwill credit (suggested 5% of monthly usage) if failures persist beyond 6 hours.
3) Authorize accelerated SDK patching cycle: canary v1.3.5 within 90 minutes; broad rollout in 6 hours pending stability.

Timeline:
- T+0: triage and apply server fallback and routing policy (if approved).
- T+2h: canary v1.3.5 to a small pool; customer to validate.
- T+6h: full rollout and monitoring.

Please ACK with approval or propose an alternative.

Neha Kapoor
Director, Customer Operations
neha_kapoor@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Live checkout spikes — requests dropping metadata causing payment failures

Alyssa — quick update and next steps.

What we changed:
- We applied a targeted traffic policy for Checkoutland at 09:10 on 5/22 to route you to the single-connection path. That removed the coalescing boundary condition and dropped error rate from ~2% to 0.1% within 30 minutes.
- Marcus pushed a canary SDK release (v1.3.5) and we validated the dechunker fix with your team in staging.
- We cut the rollout to your fleet at 01:40 on 5/24 and confirmed production throughput remained stable during the upgrade window.

Open items:
- Confirm with us whether you want us to reverse the traffic policy (recommended) or keep it for 24 hours as a safety net.
- Neha will follow up re: goodwill credit proposal if you experienced measurable revenue impact.

Please reply with a short confirmation once you see normal checkout volumes. Thanks again for the rapid collaboration — sorry for the disruption.

Rafael Mendes
